Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Li (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (NovaPay Eng Lead), Mark Huang (NovaPay ML Infra), Aisha Khan (NovaPay CTO)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Main focus: continuous batching behavior, concurrency targets, impact of queueing on p99 latency, and test plan for next benchmark run. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Current throughput numbers and gaps vs target (10k QPS goal)
- Continuous batching tweaks (max batch latency, idle flush)
- Concurrency and queueing policies (per-worker queue length, global concurrency)
- KV cache / prefix caching effects on tail latency
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for sustained throughput

Action items (covered in call): see metadata action_items field for structured list.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: ok everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — throughput updates, tuning params, and next benchmark. Priya you got any new constraints since last week?
[00:12] Priya Desai: yeah thanks Sofia. so we've been seeing intermittent p99 spikes at 200-260ms when we ramp to the mid QPS range, and peaky behaviour around 11am PST. baseline tests with your default hosted config peaked at about 6.5k QPS with 512 token average seq. goal for us is around 10k sustained, especially for the payments flows.
[00:35] Evan Li: got it. quick note, in our lab runs when continuous batching is enabled we saw 20-30% throughput lift but tail got worse at high conc, probably due to queueing in the worker local queues. we tuned max_batch_latency to 12ms and saw throughput improve but p99 moved up — there is a tradeoff.
[00:50] Mark Huang: is that the redwood runtime default? i recall default max batch latency was 8ms? also noticed the KV cash (sic) warmup sometimes confuses the numbers — startup bumps.
[01:05] Evan Li: yes default is 8ms, and good catch on the KV cash typo — we mean KV cache, the prefix cache for repeated prompts. warmup skews early metrics so we recommend warmup period in the benchmark.
[01:18] Aisha Khan: just to be clear about terms — when you say "concurrency" do you mean per-worker concurrency or global concurrent requests? that matters for our infra planning.
[01:26] Evan Li: per-worker primarily, but global concurrency interacts via the request router — there's a global queueing layer if local worker queues are full. we can control both: worker_concurrency and router_queue_limit.
[01:38] Priya Desai: our infra team prefers controlling global concurrency to avoid uneven load on GPUs. we saw one worker get saturated and latency spiked.
[01:45] Sofia Martinez: right — we typically recommend a modest worker_concurrency with a slightly larger router_queue_limit, and let continuous batching accumulate batches up to max_batch_size. that reduces overhead while keeping p50 low. but for p99-sensitive endpoints you reduce max_batch_latency and accept less throughput.
[02:05] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — sorry i missed the start, are you talking about quantization effects as well?
[02:10] Evan Li: yes, quantization helps throughput but can increase compute variance; for NovaPay we suggested int8-optimized runtime kernels. those gave 1.7x token/s improvement in our bench but changed memory layout which sometimes affects batching characteristics.
[02:26] Mark Huang: we are on GCP with T4s for now in the dev env; in prod we plan to target A100s. do you have configs tuned for mixed gpu types?
[02:36] Evan Li: we do; kernels select based on hardware and seq length. for T4 we recommend smaller batch sizes, for A100 larger. we'll include an auto-suggest matrix in the doc.
[02:48] Priya Desai: ok can you remind us of the tuning knobs you showed last week? i have notes but want to confirm defaults.
[02:55] Sofia Martinez: sure — max_batch_size, max_batch_latency (ms), worker_concurrency, router_queue_limit, kv_cache_enabled, prefix_cache_ttl, and the quantization profile (int8/int4). also batching policy: time-first vs size-first.
[03:10] Evan Li: in practice, time-first with a short max_batch_latency is best for latency-critical routes; size-first for throughput critical. our runtime supports hybrid heuristics.
[03:23] Priya Desai: running through our numbers, when we flip to size-first we saw throughput jump 40% but p99 went from ~220ms to ~375ms. unacceptable for a few endpoints.
[03:33] Aisha Khan: which endpoints are we talking about? payments authorizations are strict.
[03:36] Priya Desai: specifically the auth and fraud-score flows — they need p99 < 300ms ideally.
[03:42] Evan Li: we can run a split: keep auth on time-first with stricter latency SLO, route fraud scoring to size-first on dedicated capacity, or use model variants — a smaller model for fraud that has lower token cost.
[03:55] Mark Huang: hmm, model variant sounds interesting but we need to validate quality. can Redwood help with evals?
[04:02] Sofia Martinez: yes, we have an eval harness and can run your prompt set. we'll need sample prompts and expected outputs. Priya, you said you'd share traces?
[04:10] Priya Desai: yes i'll share two days of traces and a sampling of prompts. Mark will send them by monday.
[04:16] Evan Li: for the next benchmark we propose: 1) warmup run 10 minutes, 2) steady ramp to target QPS (10k) using realistic arrival distribution, 3) measure p50/p90/p99 and GPU util. we'll produce CSVs and a simple viz.
[04:31] Priya Desai: sounds good. question: can you simulate our bursty daily peak? our traffic has a sawtooth with bursts every 2 minutes.
[04:40] Evan Li: yes we can craft the driver to mimic that; we'll share the driver script. note: queueing behavior at burst times is most important — router_queue_limit will govern how requests are buffered vs rejected/fallback.
[04:55] Sofia Martinez: quick note about dedicated vs hosted — if you need sustained 10k with tight p99 we often recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) with autoscaling headroom. hosted can do it but you may see more variability depending on multitenant noise.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: what's the rough cost delta? we need a ballpark to justify Dedicated.
[05:15] Sofia Martinez: i'll send the updated pricing sheet; rough thumb — Dedicated for your profile may be 1.8-2.5x the pure hosted cost but with much tighter SLOs and predictable latency. depends on commit level.
[05:30] Mark Huang: can we do a short canary on Dedicated and fallback to hosted?
[05:34] Evan Li: yes, Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies; route certain routes to Dedicated and overflow to hosted, or failover on capacity pressure.
[05:42] Priya Desai: earlier you mentioned router_queue_limit — what's a good starting value?
[05:46] Evan Li: start with router_queue_limit = 128 per router instance and worker_concurrency = 16 on A100s, max_batch_size = 64, max_batch_latency = 12ms for throughput-first. For latency-first lower max_batch_latency to 6-8ms and reduce worker_concurrency to 8. These are starting points, we'll tune.
[06:10] Priya Desai: ok we'll try the throughput-first profile in staging. will that require code changes?
[06:15] Evan Li: no code change — just config in the route and runtime. we can push config via your control plane or we can apply it in the POC env.
[06:22] Aisha Khan: on security/compliance — any change with Dedicated vs hosted? we need SOC2 and SAML/SSO integrations.
[06:29] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated adds stronger isolation and customer network options (VPC peering), and we provide SOC2 docs. for SAML we support SSO via SAML/OIDC. we'll attach the security pack link after the call.
[06:40] Speaker 2: (background) is there an ETA on the quartile viz you mentioned?
[06:45] Evan Li: we'll generate quartile plots with the benchmark. expected deliverable with next run ~ 2026-05-20.
[06:52] Priya Desai: one more thing — we've seen some variance when kv cache TTL is low. what's the recommended TTL?
[06:58] Evan Li: depends on reuse pattern; for payments prompts a 30s-5m TTL often helps. too long and you risk staleness for context updates. we'll run sensitivity tests.
[07:12] Mark Huang: regarding the benchmark driver, can we run it in our GCP project to avoid cross cloud egress effects?
[07:18] Evan Li: yes recommend running the driver close to the compute to avoid network noise. we'll provide the driver container and instructions.
[07:24] Priya Desai: perfect. timeline wise, we need results before next exec sync on 2026-05-21.
[07:30] Sofia Martinez: understood — targeted deliverable 5/20, uploads to the shared drive and I'll ping you.
[07:36] Aisha Khan: any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:38] Evan Li: none — need the traces and permission to run driver in your project for the A100 run.
[07:44] Priya Desai: i'll coordinate with infra to grant temporary access. Mark will email the traces.
